stemMd: A printing press produces $850$ pages every $5$ minutes. Working at this constant rate, how many pages does the press produce in $2$ hours?
explanationMd:
Put both quantities in the same unit of time before you multiply. That single habit prevents every wrong answer offered here.

$2$ hours $= 2 \times 60 = 120$ minutes.

Now work in pages per minute:

$$\frac{850 \text{ pages}}{5 \text{ minutes}} = 170 \text{ pages per minute}$$

$$170 \times 120 = 20{,}400 \text{ pages}$$

The answer is $20{,}400$, Choice C.

A second route avoids the per-minute step: $120 \div 5 = 24$ five-minute intervals, and $850 \times 24 = 20{,}400$. Getting the same number two different ways is the cheapest check available.

A third check is a rough estimate: $850$ pages per $5$ minutes is about $10{,}000$ pages an hour, so two hours should land near $20{,}000$. That estimate alone rules out three of the four options.

distractorRationale.a: This multiplies the five-minute output by $2$, treating "$2$ hours" as two intervals of five minutes. Two hours is $24$ such intervals, not $2$.
distractorRationale.b: This uses $12$ five-minute intervals, which is one hour's worth, and so gives the output for half the stated time.
distractorRationale.d: This multiplies the per-minute rate by $150$, mis-converting $2$ hours into $150$ minutes. Two hours is $120$ minutes; $150$ minutes would be two and a half hours.

accessibilityText: A printing press produces 850 pages every 5 minutes. Find how many pages it produces in 2 hours at that constant rate. The four options are 1,700; 10,200; 20,400; and 25,500.

provenance.notes: Original item. Every distractor corresponds to a specific unit-conversion slip rather than to an arbitrary near-miss.
